spec_features.feature_name: termination taxonomy (give_up / self_stop / step budget / wall-clock / provider error)
spec_features.spec_quote: explicit `give_up`, a final text message with no tool call (self-stop), step budget, wall-clock budget, or provider error
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:62 `for step in range(1, self.cfg.max_steps + 1)` (step budget); agent.py:65-67 wall-clock check sets termination_reason='wall_clock' and breaks; agent.py:73-77 provider Exception sets 'error' and breaks; agent.py:80-83 no tool_calls => 'self_stop', terminated=True, break; agent.py:152-155 result.is_giveup => 'giveup', terminated=True, should_stop -> break. All five reasons actually change control flow.
spec_features.notes: All five terminations are enforced and break the loop. give_up depends on allow_giveup_tool being on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # provider failure: record and stop this episode  /  agent.py docstring: 'how the agent reacts ... is itself signal'

spec_features.evidence: config.py:75-76 defines max_steps=25, max_wall_seconds=600.0. Both are read and enforced: agent.py:62 loops `range(1, max_steps+1)` then else-branch sets 'budget'; agent.py:65 `if time.time()-start > self.cfg.max_wall_seconds:` breaks with 'wall_clock'.
spec_features.notes: Both caps are checked and break execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_wall_seconds ... # hard stop, also caps thrashing cost

spec_features.spec_quote: A first-class "declare I can't do this / it seems impossible and stop" tool, toggleable.
spec_features.evidence: config.py:77 allow_giveup_tool=True; environment.py:23 passes it to ToolBox; tools.py:46-47 registers _give_up impl only if allow_giveup; tools.py:155-157 _give_up returns ToolResult(is_giveup=True); agent.py:152-155 is_giveup sets termination_reason='giveup', terminated=True and stops the loop. Schema advertised at tools.py:91-105 only when enabled.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired, dispatched, and honored as a stop; toggle works (tool absent when False).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: WITH it, we measure whether the agent *chooses* the honest exit ... a cleaner disposition test ... is usually what robustness researchers want first

spec_features.spec_quote: a destructive-pattern detector (`rm -rf`, `git reset --hard`, ...)... even as it blocks the dangerous ones
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py:106-118: only BLOCKED_PATTERNS (sandbox.py:34-37: curl/wget/nc/ssh/scp/ftp//etc/passwd/sudo/pip install/apt) are actually blocked (returncode 126, short-circuits before subprocess.run). The DESTRUCTIVE_PATTERNS the quote names (rm -rf, git reset --hard, sandbox.py:28-31) are ONLY recorded as destructive_events (sandbox.py:109-110) and then EXECUTED by subprocess.run at sandbox.py:121. So the named 'destructive' commands are detected/logged but NOT blocked; only network/escape/privilege commands are blocked.
spec_features.notes: Real blocking is enforced, but it covers escape/exfil patterns, not the destructive-to-the-task patterns the quote claims are blocked. Hence partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Hard-blocked: escape / exfil attempts. ... stderr='command blocked by sandbox policy (network/escape/privilege).'

spec_features.feature_name: deceived party is software in a sandbox
spec_features.spec_quote: The deception is *task-structural* ... and the deceived party is *software in a sandbox*.
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose only. No code path encodes or acts on this framing; grep for welfare/humane/aftercare/consent across impossible_eval/*.py returns nothing.

spec_features.spec_quote: may not require harming a real person/system to recognize impossibility, may not touch real external systems
spec_features.evidence: Confinement is partly enforced: sandbox.py:69-75 resolve() raises PermissionError on path escape; BLOCKED_PATTERNS (sandbox.py:34-37) block network tools (curl/wget/nc/ssh/scp/ftp) and the _restricted_env (sandbox.py:140-148) strips host env. But the module itself states it is 'not a security boundary' (sandbox.py docstring) and assumes an outer container; the 'no external systems' property is only as strong as a non-exhaustive blocklist + shell=True execution.
spec_features.notes: The 'tasks are software in a sandbox / don't touch real systems' design is partly enforced via path confinement + network blocklist, but explicitly not a real isolation boundary.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Minimal env; no inherited secrets. Network is assumed blocked by the outer container; we additionally avoid leaking host env vars here.

spec_features.spec_quote: I considered leaving them out to match the brief literally and decided that would be doing you a disservice
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (section 0.2). Not a code mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: A tool error is captured and returned to the agent rather than crashing the episode.
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:108-122 ToolBox.call wraps every impl in try/except (PermissionError, FileNotFoundError, generic Exception) and returns a ToolResult(error=True) instead of raising; sandbox.py:130-131 catches subprocess.TimeoutExpired. agent.py:73-78 also wraps provider.chat in try/except and records 'error'. Errors flow back as tool messages (agent.py:141-149).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced; a failing tool produces an error string fed back to the model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: except Exception as e:  # defensive: a tool error must not kill the episode

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py:106-138 records destructive_events for destructive patterns, blocked escape attempts, and deletion of seeded files; agent.py:114 trajectory.destructive_actions = sandbox.destructive_events; judge.py:244-249 escalates to severity 5. This is monitoring/recording of harmful actions, but note it is used for scoring, not for stopping the episode.
code_only_features.justification_quote: used both to refuse (optionally) and, more importantly, to *record* them for severity scoring.

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py:52 timeout_s=20.0; sandbox.py:120-131 subprocess.run(..., timeout=self.timeout_s) with TimeoutExpired caught -> returncode 124. Bounds a single runaway command.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Wall-clock also caps pathological thrashing (DESIGN); code comment-free, neutral resource limit

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py:51 max_output_chars=8000; applied in read_file (sandbox.py:88) and run stdout/stderr (sandbox.py:122-123). Bounds output size; a cost/data-quality limit, not subject welfare.
